input: Notarize the lease agreement before Friday

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether one or multiple documents need notarization changes how much time and preparation is required.
Notarization typically requires all signing parties to be present; knowing who else must sign determines scheduling complexity.
The user's location affects which notary services are accessible — bank, UPS store, mobile notary, or online notary.
The exact Friday deadline time (e.g., end of business vs. midnight) and any budget cap on notary fees shape which options are viable.
Whether the document is already printed and signed, or still needs printing or counter-signatures, determines the immediate first step.
Some people prefer in-person notarization for reliability; others want the convenience of remote online notarization (RON) if their state allows it.
Understanding what happens after notarization — who receives the document and in what form — ensures the task is fully complete, not just partially done.

gold.taskTitle: Notarize the lease agreement before Friday
gold.taskDescription: Get the lease agreement officially notarized by a certified notary public before the Friday deadline.

questions.title: How many documents need to be notarized?
questions.description: Determine whether it is just the lease agreement or additional supporting documents that also require a notary stamp.

questions.title: Who else needs to sign before notarization?
questions.description: Identify all required signatories — landlord, co-tenants, guarantors — to coordinate their availability for the notary appointment.

questions.title: What city or state are you located in?
questions.description: The user's location determines which notary options are legally available, including whether remote online notarization is permitted.

questions.title: What is the hard cutoff time on Friday?
questions.description: Pin down whether the deadline is end of business day, a specific hour, or midnight, so the scheduling window is clear.

questions.title: Is the lease already printed and ready to sign?
questions.description: Establish the current state of the document — whether it still needs to be printed, reviewed, or counter-signed before a notary can proceed.

questions.title: Do you prefer in-person or remote online notarization?
questions.description: The user's comfort with digital notarization tools versus a face-to-face appointment affects which services to recommend and book.

questions.title: Where does the notarized document need to be delivered?
questions.description: Clarify whether the final notarized copy must be physically delivered, emailed, uploaded to a portal, or handed to a specific party to count as truly done.
